intro: When you feel sick, who helps you? Maybe a nurse, a doctor or a pharmacist. Around the world, people have asked the same question for thousands of years. They have built different ways of healing.

In this unit you will meet healers from the West, like Hippocrates, Florence Nightingale, Louis Pasteur and Clara Barton. You will also learn about Traditional Chinese Medicine from China and Ayurveda from India. Each tradition has its own ideas about the body.

You will see how science tests what works and what is safe. By the end, you will be able to compare traditions with respect. You will also know why it helps to tell your doctor about everything you use.
bigQuestion: How have people in different parts of the world cared for the sick, and how do we find out what really helps?

timeline.t: Hippocrates teaches in Greece that illness has natural causes
The Yellow Emperor's Classic, a key TCM book, is being put together in China
Ayurveda's Charaka Samhita is taking shape in India
Florence Nightingale leads nurses at the army hospital in Scutari
Louis Pasteur shows that germs cause spoiling
Clara Barton founds the American Red Cross
Tu Youyou wins a Nobel Prize for a malaria medicine from sweet wormwood
The World Health Organization reports on traditional medicine worldwide

words.d: reasons for something that come from the world around us, not from magic or gods
four body fluids that old Greek doctors believed had to stay in balance
a serious promise, often said out loud in front of others
keeping places clean, with clean water and safe ways to remove waste
the idea that many diseases are caused by germs
a medicine that kills bacteria or stops them from growing
a careful test of a medicine or treatment with volunteers
in TCM, a life energy that the tradition teaches flows through the body
a TCM practice where very thin needles are placed at certain points on the body
a very old healing tradition from India whose name means knowledge of life

test.q: What did Hippocrates teach about illness?
test.why: Hippocrates taught that illness has natural causes that doctors can study.

test.q: Why were the four humors replaced?
choices: New evidence showed germs and how organs work
test.why: Microscopes and careful tests gave new evidence, so the idea changed.

test.q: What is the main idea of the Hippocratic Oath?
choices: Help the sick and do no harm
test.why: The oath promises to help the sick and never harm them.

test.q: What did Florence Nightingale show with her data?
test.why: Her records and charts showed more soldiers died from sickness, and cleaning up helped.

test.q: Who founded the American Red Cross in 1881?
test.why: Clara Barton founded the American Red Cross in 1881.

test.q: Which scientist showed that germs cause spoiling?
test.why: Louis Pasteur's flask tests showed that germs cause broth to spoil.

test.q: Which medicine did Alexander Fleming discover in 1928?
test.why: Fleming discovered penicillin, one of the first antibiotics.

test.q: In a clinical trial, why does one group get a placebo?
choices: To compare it with the real medicine
test.why: A placebo has no medicine, so scientists can see if the real medicine helps more.

test.q: Which idea belongs to Traditional Chinese Medicine?
test.why: TCM teaches that qi flows along meridians. Doshas belong to Ayurveda.
Vata, pitta and kapha are the three doshas of Ayurveda.

test.q: Which practice has good evidence for helping older adults with balance?
test.why: Studies show tai chi helps older adults improve balance.

test.q: What does evidence say about acupuncture?
choices: It may help some kinds of pain for some people
test.why: Studies show it may help some kinds of pain. For many other problems the evidence is unclear.

test.q: Why should you tell your doctor about herbs and supplements?
choices: Some can change how other medicines work
It is required by the Red Cross
test.why: Some herbs can change how medicines work, and some products are not clean.

test.q: How are Western medicine, TCM and Ayurveda alike?
choices: All want to help people be well
test.why: They use different ideas and tools, but all aim to help people feel well.

test.q: What does science do when new evidence comes?
choices: Changes ideas to fit the evidence
test.why: Science changes ideas when evidence changes, like when the four humors were replaced.

write.prompt: A classmate says, old healing traditions are either all good or all bad. Do you agree? Use two or three facts from this unit, such as tai chi, acupuncture, Ayurvedic supplements or clinical trials, to explain your answer.
tips: Start with a clear claim in one sentence.
Give at least two facts from the unit and say where they came from.
Be fair and respectful to each tradition.
Use unit words like evidence, clinical trial and tradition.
End by saying why talking to a doctor matters.
